transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just been feeling tired and lacking energy all the time, really. It's been getting in the way of things.
When did you first notice it?
Since last week, I'd say.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's there all day really, but it's worse in the afternoon — I've been needing a nap most days now, which I never used to do.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
Just a real lack of energy, like I'm running on empty. I'd rate it about 3 out of 10, and I've had to stop my twice-weekly swimming, which I miss.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's not really in one place — it's just a general tiredness all over. Though I have noticed I get more short of breath than usual going up hills.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I'd say about a 3 out of 10 — my energy's that low. It's enough that I've had to give up my swimming.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It's there all day, every day, really — it doesn't come and go. It just gets worse as the day goes on, especially the afternoons.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?

A few things, yes — friends say I look pale, and I get more short of breath than usual on hills. No chest pain, no weight loss, and my bowels are fine, but I do wake up unrefreshed even after about 7 hours' sleep.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've had type 2 diabetes for about 12 years, and I've also got an underactive thyroid.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

I take metformin 500 mg twice a day, and levothyroxine 100 micrograms each morning. I've also been on omeprazole 20 mg once a day for indigestion for years, and I take ibuprofen 400 mg most days for shoulder pain — I buy that from the chemist myself.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
Yes, codeine makes me very sick.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
I'm struggling a bit, to be honest. I help my husband wash and dress in the mornings — he has Parkinson's and I'm his main carer — and that's getting harder to manage now.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Yes, it does worry me. My main worry is that I won't be able to keep caring for my husband.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
